variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen a company fail.
variants.body:
A company has gone under in {colony}. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. A business outcome should not make the people around it disappear into a convenient political slogan. Responsibility deserves an argument about stewardship, rather than a ready-made morality tale built from facts that are not known.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
